newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas softens, Transco tender has little impact.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas softens, Transco tender has little impact.

text.p: The UK spot natural gas market was fractionally softer in sentiment on Monday, traders and brokers said.
Prices in the first and second quarters of 1998 and the gas year from October 1997 were marginally lower, but many other prices were unchanged at the close of business.
The main news event of the day was the announcement by Transco of the details of its tender to sell 4.7 teraWatt hours of storage gas in August and September.

As expected, the gas will be offered both within storage terminals and at the NBP. But one player pointed out that because there will be a charge for transfer to the NBP, he expects many if not most players to take the gas in storage and sell it out next winter.

"The tender may have some impact (on prices) this week if it's going to at all," he said, but he added that some dealers, including himself, thought it likely it would have "no impact whatsoever." Certainly few players attributed the marginal weakness of prices on Monday to the tender.

The most actively traded part of the forward curve was the coming winter. Q4 traded three times at 12.575 pence and 12.60 pence a therm and Q1 traded twice at 16.45 pence. There was also some activity in Q2 98 and Q3 98.

Otherwise there was a reasonable volume of trade for the day ahead, with trades at 9.70 pence, 9.80 pence, 9.90 pence and 10.20 pence for various different volumes. The within day market saw trade at 10.20 pence. Most market participants described the day's activity as dull, with no changes seen to market fundamentals.

The IPE natural gas contract was untraded. Price signals from the exchange were mixed, with five of the 12 monthly contracts settling at higher prices than on Friday, while the other seven settled lower. But none of the price movements was large.
